<thought>Using the ESI mass spectrum, the most intense ion is at m/z 211.0764, which corresponds to a protonated molecule [M+H]+. Subtracting the proton mass gives a neutral mass of ~210.0691 Da. The isotopic pattern shows a strong M+2 peak (~33 % of the base), characteristic of a single chlorine atom (35Cl/37Cl). Accounting for one Cl (35Cl, 34.9689 Da) leaves a mass of 175.1003 Da for C, H, and O. The combination C₁₂H₁₅O (12 C + 15 H + 1 O) matches this residual mass within ~0.012 Da (≈57 ppm) and yields an integer double‑bond equivalent when the chlorine is treated as a hydrogen equivalent (DBE = 5). This formula best fits both the exact mass and the observed chlorine isotopic pattern.  

**Molecular formula:** C12H15OCl</thought>
<final_answer>C12H15OCl</final_answer>
